title: Associated graded ring of an ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq A$ an ideal; $J^0=A$, $J^{k+1}=J^kJ$, and $A/J$ is the quotient ring [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. For $n\ge0$ let $G_n=J^n/J^{n+1}$, the quotient of the $A$-module $J^n$ by its submodule $J^{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module], whose elements are the classes $a\bmod J^{n+1}$, $a\in J^n$; so $G_0=A/J$ as an abelian group. The *associated graded ring* of $A$ with respect to $J$ is the abelian group $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}G_n$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], with canonical inclusions $\iota_n:G_n\to\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$; an element $\xi=(\xi_n)_n$ is the finite sum $\sum_n\iota_n(\xi_n)$, $\xi_n$ is its *homogeneous component of degree $n$*, and the elements of $\iota_n(G_n)$ are the *homogeneous elements of degree $n$* (written $\xi_n$ for $\iota_n(\xi_n)$). Its multiplication is $(\xi\eta)_k=\sum_{n+m=k}\mu_{n,m}(\xi_n,\eta_m)$, where $\mu_{n,m}:G_n\times G_m\to G_{n+m}$ is the map $(a\bmod J^{n+1},\,b\bmod J^{m+1})\mapsto ab\bmod J^{n+m+1}$ ($a\in J^n$, $b\in J^m$); so $(a\bmod J^{n+1})\cdot(b\bmod J^{m+1})=ab\bmod J^{n+m+1}$ on homogeneous elements, and the product is biadditive. That $\mu_{n,m}$ is well defined and biadditive, that this multiplication makes $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ a commutative ring with unit $1\bmod J$ in degree $0$, and that $\iota_0:A/J\to\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is an injective ring homomorphism, is the statement recorded in `pointers`; $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is regarded as an $A/J$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] through $\iota_0$, so that $(a\bmod J)\cdot(x\bmod J^{n+1})=ax\bmod J^{n+1}$ for $a\in A$, $x\in J^n$. An ideal $\mathfrak b\subseteq\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is *homogeneous* if for every $\xi\in\mathfrak b$ and every $n\ge0$ the homogeneous component $\iota_n(\xi_n)$ lies in $\mathfrak b$.

split_report.summary: Checked against Algebra, proof of Lemma 05GH (algebra.tex 23011-23060; tags/tags: 05GH algebra-lemma-completion-Noetherian), where $\bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}$ is used as a ring, as the target of an $R/I$-algebra map from $R/I[T_1,\ldots,T_t]$, with the homogeneous ideal $\bigoplus J\cap I^n/J\cap I^{n+1}$ and homogeneous generators; Stacks has no labelled definition of the associated graded ring (grep 'associated graded' / 'Gr_' over literature/stacks-project: the notation $\text{Gr}_I(A)$ is introduced only in artin.tex line 1268, Section 07XA; graded rings in Algebra 00JL, homogeneous ideals in Algebra 00JM lines 13368-13372; the Rees algebra of Algebra 052Q / def-nagata-rees-algebra and prop-nagata-rees-graded is a different ring, $\bigoplus I^n$, not $\bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}$). Also read the two citers: lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian (step 2: $A/J$-algebra map from the polynomial ring, homogeneous pieces; step 3: $G(K)$ a homogeneous ideal, components of generators; step 4: components of degree $n$, representatives $a_j\in J^{n-d_j}$) and lem-weil-pbc-completed-module-associated-graded-generators (step 1: unit and multiplication formula on homogeneous elements; step 5: $B_n$). (a) Completeness: the old statement defined the group, the multiplication on homogeneous elements and homogeneous ideals; now written out: $G_n$ as a quotient module, the direct sum with its inclusions and components, the product of two arbitrary elements by the convolution formula $(\xi\eta)_k=\sum_{n+m=k}\mu_{n,m}(\xi_n,\eta_m)$, the unit, the $A/J$-algebra structure through $\iota_0$ with the action formula, and homogeneous ideals by components (Stacks 00JM's third equivalent form, which is the form both citers use). Small cases: $J=0$ gives $\operatorname{gr}=A$ in degree 0; $J=A$ gives the zero ring (unit $1\bmod A=0$, consistent); $A=k[x]$, $J=(x)$ gives $k[t]$; $A=\mathbf Z$, $J=(p)$ gives $\mathbf F_p[t]$. No mathematical error found in the source or the citers. (b) Claims moved out: the well-definedness and biadditivity of $\mu_{n,m}$ (formerly the parenthesis 'independent of the choices ... since $J^{n+1}J^m+J^nJ^{m+1}\subseteq J^{n+m+1}$'), the commutative ring axioms with unit $1\bmod J$, and that $\iota_0:A/J\to\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is an injective ring homomorphism (the former 'A/J is a subring' and 'it is an A/J-algebra') are the new unsplit statement node lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure, recorded in `pointers` (not in stmt_deps), flagged unreachable until a citer cites it. 'Homogeneous ideal' is a definition, not a claim (no equivalence with 'generated by homogeneous elements' is asserted, and the citers use only the components form). (c) stmt_deps (was empty): def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient (Mathlib leaf: ideals, powers $J^n$, quotient ring $A/J$, algebras) and two new Mathlib-leaf definition nodes def-weil-pbc-quotient-module (Submodule quotient, mkQ) and def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules (DirectSum, lof, component); the DAG had no node for either (searched titles, statements and mathlib_match fields of all definition nodes for direct sum / DirectSum / quotient module / Submodule.Quotient). (d) Mathlib: the earlier LeanSearch, LeanFinder and grep searches kept; added Loogle (no hit) and LeanFinder (DirectSum.GCommRing / DirectSum.commRing are the general construction, Ideal.IsHomogeneous is for internal gradings); Mathlib has no associated graded ring of an ideal (no AssociatedGraded/GradedPiece; FilteredAlgebra/Basic.lean has only the filtration classes): the definition stays a split definition node.
